title: Evolution of the atmosphere and oceans
body: The early earth had a thin atmosphere of hydrogen and helium, which was stripped off by solar winds, as happened on all the terrestrial planets. As the earth cooled, gases and water vapour were released from its interior solid earth, and continuous volcanic eruptions added more water vapour and gases. This early atmosphere largely contained water vapour, nitrogen, carbon dioxide, methane, ammonia and very little free oxygen. As the earth cooled further, the water vapour condensed; carbon dioxide dissolved in rainwater, the temperature fell further, causing more condensation and more rain. Rainwater collected in depressions and formed the oceans within 500 million years of the earth's formation. Photosynthesis evolved around 2,500-3,000 million years ago, oxygen gradually saturated the oceans, and about 2,000 million years ago oxygen began to flood the atmosphere.
